[/p][h2]Changes to Announcement Schedule[/h2][p]
The engagement for the previous announcement has noticeably declined. Most likely due to the lack of content. This isn't expected to change for quite a while, and finding teasers that don't spoil the story gets increasingly challenging as the story nears certain end points.

To adjust for this, there won't be regular announcements on the first day of the month going forward. This may change later, but for the time being they're unsustainable, and would become increasingly hollow.

For the foreseeable future, content and information will be accumulated, and announcements will be done when there is something substantial to share.

The quality of these updates are being balanced against a degree of restlessness likely to cultivate in the absence of regular posts. Just know, that unless difficulties are expressed, everything marches along at the fastest sustainable pace possible.

[/p][h2]Author's Remarks[/h2][p] Still going steady and all is well. Okay. Thanks. Bye. [/p]

notes.title: Aftermath
notes.notes:
[h2]Technical Report[/h2][p]
As requested, the next episode was released as is. There were a few weeks taken to get everything migrated to a patch and fully tested. Some things were not as stable as originally thought, and certain features had to be postponed.

[/p][h3]Chapter Selection[/h3][p]
The main feature that didn't pass testing in the eleventh hour was a basic chapter select option. Many anticipated problems for players occurred as a result of its absence, and it remains one of the next priorities. It will likely see a few more iterations before release, and will be a hard requirement before next episode.

Now that release support is winding down, work on this can begin again.

[/p][h3]Improved Save Data[/h3][p]
Adjacent to this, there are a lot of issues with the way save data works. The underlying issues here also need to be solved as part of chapter selection.

The improved layout is expected to make save games less prone to certain types of corruption. Not everything, but it will likely avoid a fair number of common issues.

The added metadata will also open up what can be provided in the UI, and include more information about the save itself.

[/p][h3]Puzzles[/h3][p]
A strong discussion consensus, and numerous issue reports, express that many of the puzzles in specific areas were more of a drag on the story, rather than an intermission. More hints were added, and removal of red herrings were done to alleviate some friction, as this wasn't the intended experience.


[/p][h2]Author's Remarks[/h2][p]
There is not enough spoiler free content yet that is fully rendered, and can be presented as teaser material this month.

[/p][h3]Words of Gratitude[/h3][p]
Big thank you to everyone who reported issues. Your efforts have contributed a lot to the stability of the newest episode. 

There were also requests for quality of life improvements which are being taken into consideration.

Hope you enjoyed Decay part 1/2!
[/p]

[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/5960bc4d7c299181413a8ed9475826c34c1bc7ac.png"][/img]
[/p][h1]Author Comments[/h1][p]
[/p][h3]Re-vote[/h3][p]
There was significant interest in re-voting for releasing [b]Episode 3: Decay (part 1/2)[/b] alone.

It seems like many asking for a re-vote felt they didn't have enough information previously. This time I've done my best to really hammer home everything relevant.


[/p][h3]Information Recap[/h3][p]
[b]Episode 3: Decay (part 1/2)[/b] is complete. It ends on a cliffhanger for [b]Episode 4: Decay (part 2/2)[/b] which is not complete. 

[b]Episode 3: Decay (part 1/2)[/b]'s quality will neither improve nor decrease regardless of it being released alone or with [b]Episode 4: Decay (part 2/2)[/b].
 
It cannot be rushed as it is already complete. 
It won't become better as it is already complete.

[b]E3: Decay (part 1/2):[/b]

 Is complete.
 Is roughly 6 hours long.
 Has 1 ending.
 Has 1 cliffhanger (Before episode 4).
 Has 4 dead-ends / fail states.
[b]E4: Decay (part 2/2):[/b]

 Is fully written.
 Is in development.
 Will be in development for a very long time.
[b]E3: Burial:[/b]

 Is fully written.
 Development has NOT started.
 Does NOT connect to, nor share any content with Decay.
Here is an image of what the Decay branch looks like as of right now.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/15678bcaaa1ce7cc478a0ac3dcb3d95f4e9bab71.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]The Cliffhanger[/h3][p]
Neither Episode 1 nor 2 ended on a cliffhanger.

While the overarching narrative remains unfinished, both episodes successfully concluded the part of the story they set out to tell. 

This is not the case with [b]Episode 3: Decay (part 1/2)[/b] which cuts off abruptly.

It is possible to play the game from start to finish if you go for a specific ending. Otherwise the story builds up and cuts off without a satisfying conclusion. All the pay off is in episode 4, which is still in development.


[/p][h3]Development Time[/h3][p]
I can't give an accurate estimate for how long [b]Episode 4: Decay (part 2/2)[/b] is going to take. Adapting the story to game form isn't easily measured, and I'd rather not set myself up to fail by randomly guessing at it.

Information that takes a couple lines of exposition to convey in writing, might take 2 minutes in-game, or it might take 20 minutes. This depends entirely on whether the game info dumps at you, or lets you roam around experiencing things for yourself. Latter means more gameplay, backgrounds, CGs, items, events, available actions, etc... basically more everything, and much more work.

All I know is that it's going to be a while. It could easily be another year.


[/p][h3]"Author's Wishes" and Addressing Common Concerns[/h3][p]
It has come to light that some players had voted based on what they mistakenly believed I wanted.

The only thing I wanted was to know if people would take issue with a cliffhanger.

I had some hesitation about releasing the episode knowing how much people hate cliffhangers. Other than that, I do not have any strong feelings about it one way or the other, as it doesn't affect me. I'm not the one playing it. You are.

The vote was, and still is, only about whether you can handle what might likely be an unsatisfying cliffhanger until episode 4 releases and finishes the story.

I've made a point to be less hyperbolic this time around, as it seems to confuse rather than amuse.


[/p][h1]Voting[/h1][p]
Do you want [b]Episode 3: Decay (part 1/2)[/b] to be released, or do you want to wait until [b]Episode 4: Decay (part 2/2)[/b] is also completed?

Vote by leaving a comment, or by badging [url="https://steamcommunity.com/app/2378900/discussions/0/594016333228728410/"]this months discussion topic[/url].

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/0c52223aaa700fee5e5151fa63283846da83e866.png"][/img] [b]Poetry[/b]

I resent cliffhangers to the point I'd rather wait another year or so for both episodes to be released together.

notes.title: Questions & Answers
notes.notes:
[h1]Author Comments[/h1][p]
All is well. Still making content without issues. [b]Episode 4: Decay (part 2/2)[/b] is coming along nicely.
 
Last time you were given the option to leave questions about the game and story so far. Some have been combined, and others reworded for more concise answers.

If you're not interested in the Q&A, skip to the end, there's something I want to ask you.


[/p][h1]Q&A Author Responses[/h1][p]
[/p][h3]Q: How does one pronounce Leyley?[/h3][p]A: Lay-lay. "Lay" as in "Lay down."

[/p][h3]Q: Merch when??[/h3][p]A: We're in discussions regarding contracts and licensing and logistics and other legal hoopla that needs to be dealt with. It'll be a while but it'll happen.

[/p][h3]Q: You mentioned the possible re-release of your old game jam novels. Which ones? When?[/h3][p]A: Not even god knows. Thank you for all the interest.

[/p][h3]Q: What inspired The Coffin of Andy and Leyley? How did you come up with the story?[/h3][p]A: This was one of the most asked questions. Luckily I've already answered it in detail [url="https://store.steampowered.com/news/app/2378900/view/4453592738017838121?l=english"] here[/url].

[/p][h3]Q: Is it okay to refer to you by your old screen name?[/h3][p]A: Nemlei was a company name. It was acquired and discontinued. It's like calling me Coca-Cola, I don't feel any way about it. But still, thank you. Your concern warms my heart.

I don't have any current usernames, so I just go by "author".

[/p][h3]Q: People have branded this as the "incest game" despite it having a lot more to it. How does it feel?[/h3][p]A: Their loss. I'm glad not everyone has such a shallow, one-note interpretation, because this burning garbage heap is a symphony!

[/p][h3]Q: Do you think your audience is more male or female?[/h3][p]A: The target demographic is women who enjoy true crime shows, gothic romance, and dark comedy. I've no idea who showed up though, and it doesn't matter. Everyone is welcome to give me money!

[/p][h3]Q: Explicit sex hentai porn NSFW scene when???????[/h3][p]A: Never.

[/p][h3]Q: What does Andrew study?[/h3][p]A: Pedantry.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/7921c17f8c8ef95d9fa735d406f245fc5b9cab43.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]Q: What determines the color of someone's soul in the game?[/h3][p]A: Great question! Find out in Decay.

[/p][h3]Q: Is Andrew lying about his nightmares?[/h3][p]A: No, but he does exaggerate the frequency of them.

[/p][h3]Q: Did the Lady in 302 actually try to shoot Andrew?[/h3][p]A: Yes. She lunged for the nailgun but didn't make it in time.

[/p][h3]Q: Does Ashley and/or Andrew have \[cluster B type personality disorder]?[/h3][p]A: Shoehorning the characters into real-life diagnoses would only serve to diminish the narrative, and cause contradictions in the way their symptoms would or wouldn't manifest. Rather than seeing their behavior through the lens of this or that affliction, it's more fruitful to analyze the cause and effect of in-universe events.

[/p][h3]Q: Do you do anything with the batteries from episode 1?[/h3][p]A: Yes.

[/p][h3]Q: Is The Coffin of Andy and Leyley related to any other games? Is there a shared universe your games take place in?[/h3][p]A: No.

[/p][h3]Q: What inspired the character names?[/h3][p]A: A google search for the most common names in the 90s.

[/p][h3]Q: Is Ashley disinterested in sex?[/h3][p]A: Rather than disinterested, she doesn't want to grow up. Sex doesn't accommodate her fantasy of "Andy and Leyley", which is a dynamic where Andrew nurtures her unconditionally. The crux of their enmeshment is Ashley projecting all her unmet needs (platonic and sexual alike) onto Andrew, while expecting him to be a safe object that never reciprocates or asks anything of her. The "troubles ahead" shown by the trinket were what they were for a reason.

[/p][h3]Q: Why are you making Decay first? It sucks ass![/h3][p]A: Burying one's problems and pretending everything is hunky-dory doesn't solve anything. In fact, it often makes matters worse. Although unpleasant, true \[CHAOS AND MAYHEM!!!] can only be achieved by unearthing the root cause of one's issues and addressing the underlying decay.

[/p][h3]Q: How tall are Ashley and Andrew?[/h3][p]A: Ashley is small and tiny. Andrew is tall and whiny.

The talking sprites are not at all representative of their heights, as they're leveled for readability. In the CGs you can see Andrew pretty much towers over Ashley, despite him hunching down a lot of the time and her wearing heels.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/cacfd274cb508ef1355e7beac13365cce921ae1c.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]Q: "What's the size of Andrews pp"[/h3][p]A: PP be big.

[/p][h3]Q: What's the size of Ashley's awesome fat tits?[/h3][p]A: Smaller than advertised.

[/p][h3]Q: Which character do you hate the most?[/h3][p]A: If I'm not entertained by at least some aspect of a character, I don't write them. Therefore there isn't really one I'd scorn. 

[/p][h3]Q: Who is your favorite character?[/h3][p]A: The overall narrative is more fun than any singular character. Since the cast has been written to build upon one another, none of them would work in isolation.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/d98445cf34fd9bebc0bc3599aa6bacb1776f91aa.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]Q: What did mom want to talk to Andrew about?[/h3][p]A: This is a mildly interesting plot beat that showcases their similarity.
Both mom and Andrew spent the day assessing the situation. Both arrived to the same conclusion: Duo leaves quietly, and everyone pretends they were never there. Their reasons were different due to knowing different things, but essentially they both wanted to avoid drawing attention.

Mother wanted to convey this plan to Andrew, though it would've been wrapped up in a sob story about how hard she had it, and lies how she didn't know what went on at the apartment. They'd talk more about how Andrew and Ashley should "start their own lives already", the subtext being: "Get lost and stay lost". Should Andrew pretend to buy all of it, he'd leave with Ashley the next morning and never contact the parents again.

As to why Ashley can't be present for the talk; She'd call bullshit, making the pretense of the conversation impossible (both mom and Andrew need to lie about what's happening to feel better about it). But as seen in the game, the situation escalates before anyone can get a word in. Because of this, mom's plan changes to that seen in the Olive Branches gag. What little goodwill remained for her shitty kids has been irreversibly exhausted.

[/p][h3]Q: Are "Olive branches" endings canon?[/h3][p]A: Everything seen in the Olive Branches gag is canon except Andrew's behavior. Everyone else is in-character, and following the game's canon plot.

[/p][h3]Q: Why did the organ trafficking ring allow the parents to leave?[/h3][p]A: Their operation did not allow for force at that point in time.

[/p][h3]Q: You've shown a lot of teasers that take place in flashbacks. Will the majority of the next episode take place in the past?[/h3][p]A: That's just me avoiding spoilers for the main plot.

[/p][h3]Q: Will these same flashback scenes be in Burial too?[/h3][p]A: They aren't relevant in Burial. You can only see them in Decay.

notes.title: Looking Back
notes.notes:
[p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/1739dc1184508dd3fd4206b43fcd4d12659b7f8c.png"][/img]
[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/7223989369aa56f197ad2636d22b963fe4624515.png"][/img]
[/p][h3]Author Commentary[/h3][p]
The year comes to a close, making this a fitting moment to reflect back on how this game's development got started in the first place.

For a few years before The Coffin of Andy and Leyley, I had been dabbling in making visual novels as a hobby by entering visual novel jams. These were month long jams with no specific goals other than to create a visual novel from start to finish. I entered maybe once a year for... uhhh?? four years? I don't remember, and you don't care. My point here is that it was enough so that I noticed a pattern...

If a jam allowed additional gameplay in the visual novel, the entries utilizing it were often among the most played ones. "Huh." thought little ol' me, and schemed a wicked scheme. The next jam that came around (and I had time to enter) was Nanoreno, and time had come to test my hypothesis. 

I only had a month, so I knew from the start the story had to be a "bottle episode", as in the whole story must be contained within one location to save time, and limit how much art I needed to make.

So who were the characters, why were they there, and why wouldn't they switch locations? The easiest answer was the classic "they're locked in and must escape" which is a story everyone and their dog has written at some point. Whatever, it's just a game jam I thought, and carried on.

Then came the characters, at first Ashley was going to be a silent protagonist named Player (yeah, you read that right). I wanted to toy with the idea that players tend to do the most unhinged things when allowed. So there'd be the Player, and one support character whose sole purpose was to spout exposition, and react to the player doing player things. Oh, the humor that would ensue.

There is one small remnant of this idea still in the game. It's at the very beginning when the player wakes Andrew up. He explains something, and "Player" responds with an emoji bubble thing, and Andrew then says "Quit your complaining!" despite the fact that Ashley hadn't really complained out loud. Now, imagine if the entire game was like this........... It would've sucked [i]so[/i] bad. I dropped the concept pretty much right away.

This original concept is also why the narrator addresses "you" (the Player), instead of being in pure third person or first person point of view. I did enjoy this game master type format though, so even after making Ashley an actual character, I kept it.

Since Ashley was now a character, she needed to have a story. Cue the whole childhood incident (again, generic, but whatever it's a game jam). This also elevated Andrew to a character status, rather than a mere exposition spouter. Great! Now I knew who they were, and had a story to tell other than "unhinged room escape". (Which is a game I'd still want to play, as long as it isn't made by me.)

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/13e55bcdcdb0291feeb87c29cd97b7198130409e.png"][/img]
[i]This is the first ever sketch I made of the two. Almost final design straight out the bag lol.[/i]


[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/2accd0afa001051ff303e22831495cecc534cf7b.png"][/img]
[i]This was me still figuring out the UI. I don't remember what was the idea behind having the names off to the side, but thankfully I decided against it.[/i]


I drafted rather lengthy character sheets for the duo, as the more I wrote, the more they revealed themselves to be curious little jerks, with a lot going on between them. The story formed almost on its own after that. I knew I couldn't go too in-depth though, as the game jam imposed a hard time limit. So I shelved most of it thinking "well maybe I'll tell this story later on my own time", and left a sequel bait at the end of the story, to give myself an opening to get back to it "one day" that I assumed would never come. And also to give myself time to see if there really even was an interesting story to tell, or if this was one of those "really cool idea!!!"s that emerge out of the blue, but rot away as soon as you sit down to write them. If you're a fellow storyteller, you know what I'm talking about.

Leaving an "in" to continue later is something I've done plenty before. I might very well get back to my other game jam novels one day, which is part of the reason I took them down. For now though, there is no room for such endeavors, as The Coffin of Andy and Leyley must be completed, and will remain the sole priority until then.

Back to my "visual novels with gameplay perform better than pure visual novels" -hypothesis! I entered the game jam with my corny-ass bottle episode organ harvesting edgelord romp, and lo' and behold!! 

It [i]did[/i] gain more attraction than my other (gameplay-less) visual novels! In fact, it gains enough momentum to leave the visual novel scene. The new influx of people turns my data useless, and the hypothesis goes out the window. So in the end, was it the gameplay that attracted people? Or was it purely the oh, so scandalously unhealthy relationship the duo has? You tell me.

Somehow the game got caught in a shitflinging contest between the self-appointed morality police, and the people sick and tired of being told what kind of fiction they're allowed to read.

Suddenly, life gave me two choices, much like a visual novel would.

Do I take the game down to appease the people telling me to kill myself?
Or do I create the story I already wanted to create and get paid for it?

Boy oh boy, what a dilemma. I contemplated it for all of two nano seconds!

I dug out all the stuff I had shelved, and soon had the draft of the full story all ready to go. I went over it a few times, deemed it to be a lot of fun, and begun production of the full game. Episode 2 released on Steam in October 2023, and The Coffin of Andy and Leyley wrecked havoc across social media! And I thought there was a shitstorm before? HAHAHHAHAHA!!!!

And here we are now.

I want to thank you, my dear audience, for all your support. And I also want to thank the people who tirelessly pissed and moaned about some crappy indie game for months and months and months, helping it gain popularity beyond my comprehension. I would've never, ever gotten this far if it wasn't for you! The kinder thanks goes to the audience though, obviously. Thank you for weathering the storm with me, I hope you'll like the terrible little story you've helped to subsist.

The development continues, unchanged. I can't wait to show you the next episode. It's just awful, I really like it! Hope you will too.

Have a wonderful end of the year,


- The Author of The Coffin of Andy and Leyley, Your Least Favorite Person.
[/p]

[/p][h3]Major Revisions[/h3][p]
The gameplay portion that was recently completed was fully reviewed this month, and special attention is needed for handling the new division between episode 3A and 4.

Previously, the amount of game related content needed to execute on the script expanded way beyond its container, and it was decided that a large part of episode 3A should be split off into a fourth episode. However problems with finding a graceful transition point persisted with no good solution. There is no satisfying or sensible end point between the episodes currently, and it is very likely the case that these two episodes (3A and 4) require being shipped together as a result.

The author has stepped back to re-evaluate the best approach.

While we labored optimistically towards providing a release date, a hard decision to err on the side of quality has been made. Keeping to an arbitrary deadline with what exists currently, would hurt the final result.

The development cycle will be prolonged by some additional months to address this entangling work between the next two episodes, and to avoid development burnout.


[/p][h3]Work Remaining[/h3][p]
With previous projections having partly gone out the window, it may not be insightful to continue with the content estimations just yet. As it isn't known yet if episode 3A and its follow-up episode 4 are released at the same time, or if episode 3A can be delivered before episode 4's completion.

Once some details shake out, there might be a better picture of how this dilemma will resolve.

Additional information and consideration is needed to resume providing the graphs for how this situation is moving forward. Work still steadily continues, but the horizon has moved out of view for the time being.

The next release is going to be considerably larger than the previous two combined, and it will simply take longer to finish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/43894685/f63e9c4dc5877f1435a81f645990c0a29b2c4ec4.png[/img]

I do believe you'll like the variety of outcomes. Though some of you will intensely despise them.
